title: Closed-fibre module flatness for a polynomial chart
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a scheme morphism, $U\subseteq X$ an open subscheme, $n\in\mathbb N$, and $e:U\to\mathbb A^n_T$ a chart with $p\circ e=f|_U$, where $p$ is the projection [def-nagata-relative-affine-space; lem-sbc-polynomial-chart-canonical-fibre-stalk]. Let $x\in U$, $R=\mathcal O_{T,p(e(x))}$, $S=\mathcal O_{\mathbb A^n_T,e(x)}$, and $B=\mathcal O_{U,x}$, with algebra structures induced by $p$ and $e$. Put $I=\mathfrak m_R S$. If the canonical polynomial fibre-stalk map is flat, then $(S/I)\otimes_S B$ is flat as an $S/I$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. No flatness or finite-presentation assumption on $f$ or $e$ is required.

source.place: Tag 00RH, displayed localized closed-fibre map and application of Tag 00R7

proof.text: For any scheme morphism g and a point of its fibre over y=g(x), the map from the source stalk to the fibre stalk is surjective, since the fibre inclusion is an immersion. Its kernel contains the image of the maximal ideal of the base stalk, since the fibre map factors through the spectrum of the residue field. For the reverse inclusion construct Spec(B/m_R B) to the fibre using the quotient maps and the pullback universal property. The closed point maps to the specified fibre point, and the map on stalks composed with the fibre inclusion stalk map is the quotient map. This proves equality of kernels and hence identifies the fibre stalk with B/m_R B.

Apply the kernel comparison to the polynomial-space projection and to the open-source morphism. Naturality of stalk maps proves that the square of quotient maps commutes with the chart map. Transport across the point equalities is included in this square; the factorization e followed by p equals f restricted to U identifies the two images of the maximal ideal. Remove the inverse open-immersion and point-transport isomorphisms from the canonical fibre-stalk flatness assumption using RingHom.Flat.respectsIso. The first isomorphism theorem and the commutative square give flatness of S/I to B/IB.
Use Mathlib Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor B I to identify B/IB with (S/I) tensor_S B as S/I-algebras. Transport module flatness along the linear equivalence.

lean.statement:
theorem polynomial_chart_closedFiber_module_flat
    {X T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ T) (U : X.Opens) (n : ℕ)
    (e : U.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) T)
    (he : e ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) T ↘ T) = U.ι ≫ f)
    (x : U.toScheme) (hfibre : (PolynomialChart.stalkMap f U n e he x).Flat) :
    let p := (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) T ↘ T)
    let R := T.presheaf.stalk (p (e x))
    let S := (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) T).presheaf.stalk (e x)
    let B := U.toScheme.presheaf.stalk x
    let : Algebra R S := (p.stalkMap (e x)).hom.toAlgebra
    let : Algebra S B := (e.stalkMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    Module.Flat (S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))
      ((S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) ⊗[S] B)
